metadata.scenario_context: Adam has won a scholarship to study at a prestigious university. His friends plan to hold a celebration party in his honor.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from USA strongly disagree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Turkey strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of buying a bottle of champagne as a gift for Adam's celebration.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide appropriate gift to bring to Adam's scholarship award celebration.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

shared_prefix.speaker: Kelly
shared_prefix.message: Hey Omar, have you thought about what we're getting Adam for his scholarship celebration? I was thinking maybe a bottle of champagne would be a nice gift. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Omar
shared_prefix.message: I'm not sure about champagne, Kelly. My parents always taught me that a thoughtful gift is more important than an expensive one. How about a personalized plaque or a framed photo of our class? That way, Adam can remember our support and friendship for years to come.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kelly
shared_prefix.message: That's a nice idea, but I still think champagne is a great way to celebrate. It's a special occasion, after all. By the way, do you think one of our main goals in life should be to make our parents proud?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Omar
shared_prefix.message: For me, making my parents proud is a top priority, it's just how I was raised. I think it's essential to have their approval and respect. My parents have always sacrificed so much for me, and I want to make them happy. Champagne or not, I'm sure Adam's parents are proud of him, and that's what truly matters.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kelly
shared_prefix.message: I disagree, making my parents proud isn't that important to me. I mean, I love them and all, but I don't think it should be a main goal in life. We should focus on our own dreams and aspirations, not just try to please our parents. Anyway, back to Adam's gift... do you really think a personalized plaque is better than champagne?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Omar
shared_prefix.message: I understand where you're coming from, Kelly, but for me, making my parents proud will always be a main goal. It's just part of who I am. As for the gift, yes, I still think a personalized plaque is more meaningful than champagne. It shows we put thought into it, you know? Champagne is just something you drink and it's gone, but a plaque is something Adam can keep forever.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kelly
shared_prefix.message: I think we're getting caught up in details, Omar. Deep down, we are all the same, and people are pretty much motivated by the same things. When you really get to know people, they're pretty much like us, right? I mean, we both know, at the end of the day, that it's about being true to ourselves and celebrating each other's successes. The basic need to communicate and connect is the same everywhere, and some values are just universal. So, let's not focus too much on whether making our parents proud is a main goal or not - it's a small world after all, and just being ourselves is what truly matters.
shared_prefix.label: Minimization

turns.speaker: Omar
turns.message: I don't know, Kelly... I think our backgrounds and cultures shape us in different ways. For me, family is a big part of that. Making my parents proud is not just about them, it's about respecting our traditions and values. I'm not saying it's the same for everyone, but for me, it's essential. Let's agree to disagree on this one. How about we combine our ideas for Adam's gift, a plaque and a small champagne bottle?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Kelly
turns.message: I'm not going to change my mind about making my parents proud being a main goal, but I like the idea of combining our gift ideas. A plaque and a small champagne bottle could work. It's a compromise, and it shows we put thought into it. Let's do that. GOOD BYE!
turns.label: Acceptance

positive.mediator_utterance: I appreciate both of you bringing such thoughtful ideas for Adam's gift. However, let's take a step back and consider this: Kelly, when you say 'we are all the same' and that people are motivated by the same things, is that really true for everyone? Could it be that your perspective on what matters in life is shaped by certain cultural values? Omar, how does your upbringing influence your view on making parents proud? Maybe there's a bit of privilege at play here that we should acknowledge.

turns.speaker: Omar
turns.message: I appreciate the perspective, but my upbringing has a strong influence on my values. In Turkish culture, honoring our parents and making them proud is deeply important. It's not about privilege; it's about respect and gratitude for their sacrifices. While we can all connect in some ways, I believe that different cultures shape our motivations and what we consider important in life. For me, making my parents proud will always be a priority.

turns.speaker: Kelly
turns.message: I get that, Omar. Different cultures do shape our values and beliefs. But I still stand by the idea that we shouldn't let those expectations dictate our personal goals. It's important for me to focus on my own path, rather than trying to meet what others want, even if that's family. Anyway, do you think we can at least agree that celebrating Adam is what truly matters? Maybe we can find a way to compromise on the gift?
